title: HOA Rules for Painting Your House: What to Check First
description: Most Fort Bend County HOAs require written approval before you repaint your exterior, often from an approved color list. Here's what to submit, what gets denied, and how to avoid fines.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: most HOAs in Sugar Land, Katy, Richmond and the rest of Fort Bend County require written approval before you repaint your home's exterior, even if you're keeping the same colors in some communities. You'll usually submit a request form with your color names, color codes and which part of the house each goes on. Then you wait for the architectural committee to approve it. Painting without approval can lead to fines and an order to repaint.

Step 1: Find Your HOA's Rules

Look for your community's deed restrictions, design guidelines or architectural standards. They're usually on the HOA or management company's website or resident portal. Look for:

  • Whether repainting requires approval, or only color changes do

  • An approved color palette, often from a specific paint brand

  • Rules about body, trim, accent and front door colors

  • Rules about painting brick or stone

  • Rules about matching or differing from neighboring houses

Step 2: Submit an Architectural Request

Most HOAs want a request form that includes:

  • The brand, color name and color code for each color

  • Where each color goes: body, trim, fascia, shutters, front door, garage door

  • Physical color samples or swatches, if required

  • Sometimes a photo of your house and of the neighbors' houses

Approval can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks, depending on how often the committee meets. Submit early so your project start date isn't held up.

Requests That Commonly Get Denied

  • Bright or highly saturated body colors

  • Colors identical or too similar to an adjacent home, in communities that require variety

  • Painting brick or stone that the guidelines say must stay natural

  • Incomplete forms missing color codes or locations

Step 3: Keep the Approval Letter

Once approved, keep the letter and share it with your painter. If the HOA approved specific color codes, those exact colors should go on the house. Substituting a "close" color from another brand can cause problems.

How a Painter Can Help

An experienced local painter knows which communities have strict palettes and what usually gets approved. Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need HOA approval to repaint my house the same color?

Some HOAs don't require approval for an exact same-color repaint; others do. Check your guidelines, and when in doubt, submit a request.

What happens if I paint my house without HOA approval?

Typically a violation notice, possible fines, and a requirement to repaint in approved colors at your cost.

Does the HOA need to approve my front door color?

Often yes. Many guidelines treat front doors and shutters as accent colors that need approval too.
